01

Retention collapse

Skill-based matching loses half its users by week three.

Skill tells you who can play. It does not tell you who will come back. The people who leave first make it look like there is nobody worth playing with, and the ones who stay leave later because the conversation never worked.

22%

D30 retention · skill-matching platforms

Observed band across comparable services

65%

D30 target · conversation-led matching

Zenith hypothesis from closed-beta simulation. Not yet measured in market.

Three toxicity patterns

You can make the match. If the conversation breaks, the platform breaks.

01 · Abuse

  • Slurs and demeaning speech
  • Trigger words that must leave voice chat immediately

02 · Ghosting

  • No reply, or mute and vanish
  • Matching cost spent, no revenue event

03 · Catfishing

  • Fake profiles, pulled off to another game
  • Payment-fraud traffic noise

02

The product

Sign up, check in, matched — twenty-eight seconds.

The moment you open a mobile game, a mate with a 92-point conversation-compatibility score is already waiting. One state check-in starts the session.

In the app

The core design decision: ask how you are before asking what you play. State first, genre second.

03

State Match

Disposition is fixed. State changes. We read both.

Trait · who am I as a mate

  • Big Five personality
  • Preferred genres
  • Voice score
  • Tone — formal, casual, emoji frequency

State · what do I need right now

  • Mood: cheer me on, keep it easy, focus, challenge
  • Session length
  • Mic on or off
  • Avoid a heavy tone
Layer 01Trait embedding — speech and personality as a 768-dimension vector
Layer 02State affinity — five-axis multimodal mapping of the check-in
Layer 03Rejection learning — reinforcement on why sessions were declined
Layer 04Risk gating — exposure only after the safety filter clears

Chemistry and risk

Chemistry can read 92. If risk sits above the line, we still do not send it.

92.4

Conversation compatibility / 100

Under 80 re-match · 80 to 90 shown as a candidate · above 90 matched immediately

0.4

Relationship risk / 10 — lower is safer

Under 2.0 exposed · 2 to 5 conditional · above 5 blocked automatically

120ms

Check-in to recommended cards

Safe Match Mode. If your last session ran sharp, Zenith says so before the next match and offers a calmer mate instead — protection placed before the introduction, not after the report.

Why the US first

  • The same visible-transaction behaviour
  • Low localisation cost

Why Japan next

  • Second-highest mobile ARPU in the world
  • Gacha culture — a market already fluent in paying for feeling

Sources: Newzoo 2025 Global Games Market, IMARC, Statista.

Where we sit

Plenty of products match well. None do conversation and safety together.

Skill marketplaces

  • Matching is solved
  • Relationship-risk control is absent

Community voice apps

  • Group voice, not one-to-one matching
  • No opinion on who you should meet

LFG tools

  • They fill tonight's lobby
  • Built for teams, not relationships

Zenith takes the corner nobody occupies: relationship matching with risk control underneath it.
